newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close lower after day of drift.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close lower after day of drift.

text.p: Equities in Paris finished lower on Thursday after an indecisive day in which the CAC index drifted in a 21-point range. The CAC dipped below 2,600 points but recovered to trade above this support level.
Traders said the market lacked big themes to drive the index higher and slim hopes of an interest rate cut were snuffed out when the Bank of France left rates unchanged at a money market tender.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 9.58 points or 0.37 percent at 2,607.97. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 14 at 2,606 from Wednesday's close.
Volume was a light 4.84 billion francs.
"The session was pretty well marked by a consolidation. People were taking profit," said one trader.
The market was cautious ahead of Friday's U.S. producer price and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT. Some are expecting a further U.S. interest rate rise in May to pre-empt inflation.
If it falls below 2,600 and 2,590 points, the CAC could retrace to 2,550 before attracting buyers or triggering short covering.

Synthelabo shares added 7.35 percent to 672 francs, helped by a Goldman Sachs upgrade to outperfrom from in-line performance. Other brokerages have upped their forecasts after an analysts meeting on Tuesday.
Sanofi shares gained 2.62 percent to 549 in sympathy.
Canal Plus added 2.3 percent to 1,110, boosted by an optimismic analysts meeting earlier this week.
Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux will set merger terms at 41 Suez shares for 20 Lyonnaise at Friday's special board meetings at the two merger partners, a source close to the talks told Reuters.
